module_title: Continents, Oceans, and Major Landforms - Basic Understanding
introduction: The surface of the Earth is not uniform; approximately 71% of it is covered by water (Oceans), and 29% is covered by land (Continents). At this beginner level, we will memorize the continents and oceans in order of their size and understand the basic differences between primary landforms.

core_concepts.title: The 7 Continents (In Decreasing Order of Size)
core_concepts.description: Continents are massive, continuous expanses of land. From largest to smallest: 1. Asia (Largest & most populous), 2. Africa, 3. North America, 4. South America, 5. Antarctica (The frozen 'White Continent'), 6. Europe, 7. Australia (The smallest continent).

core_concepts.title: The 5 Oceans (In Decreasing Order of Size)
core_concepts.description: Oceans are the vast bodies of continuous saltwater. The order is: 1. Pacific Ocean (Largest and deepest), 2. Atlantic Ocean, 3. Indian Ocean, 4. Southern (Antarctic) Ocean, 5. Arctic Ocean (Smallest and shallowest).

core_concepts.title: Major Landforms
core_concepts.description: 1. Mountains: Naturally elevated land masses with a steep slope and a sharp peak. 2. Plateaus: Elevated flat lands that rise sharply above the surrounding area (also called 'Tablelands'). 3. Plains: Vast, flat, and low-lying landmasses, usually formed by the fertile silt deposited by river systems.

core_concepts.title: The Uniqueness of the Indian Ocean
core_concepts.description: The Indian Ocean holds a unique geographical distinction: It is the 'only' ocean in the world named after a specific country (India). Its shape is roughly triangular.

important_entities.name: Eurasia
important_entities.significance: Geographically, Europe and Asia are not separated by an ocean; they form a single, massive continuous landmass known as 'Eurasia'. They are traditionally considered separate continents divided by the 'Ural Mountains' and the 'Ural River' in Russia.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common geographical confusion: 'Australia' is both a country and a continent (often called an Island Continent). However, when you combine Australia, New Zealand, and the thousands of small islands in the Pacific (Micronesia, Polynesia, Melanesia), the entire region is officially referred to as 'Oceania'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use the word PAISA (Money): Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic.

exam_strategy_tips: SSC and Railway exams frequently ask: 'Which mountain range separates Europe from Asia?' The answer is always the 'Ural Mountains'.
